CheckTitle: Privileged Microsoft first-party administration apps require explicit user assignment
Description: Microsoft Entra **service principals** for privileged first-party administration tools (Azure PowerShell, Azure CLI, Graph Explorer, Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools, etc.) have **appRoleAssignmentRequired** set to `true`, restricting sign-in to explicitly assigned users and groups.
Risk: These Microsoft apps hold broad delegated permissions (e.g. `Directory.AccessAsUser.All`). By default **any user** can sign in. After compromising any account an attacker uses these tools to **enumerate the directory and exfiltrate data**. A missing service principal is also open because Entra creates it on first sign-in with assignment not required.

Code.Other:
1. If the service principal is missing, create it:
   - PowerShell: `New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId <appId>`
   - Azure CLI: `az ad sp create --id <appId>`
2. In the Microsoft Entra admin center (https://entra.microsoft.com) go to Identity > Applications > Enterprise applications
3. Remove the "Application type == Enterprise Applications" filter so Microsoft applications are listed
4. Search by appId and select the app
5. Go to Users and groups and assign the admin users/groups that need access
6. Go to Properties > set "Assignment required?" to **Yes** > Save

**Warning**: once enforced, unassigned users (including the identity running Prowler in browser/Azure CLI auth modes) can no longer sign in with these tools. Assign the scanning identity and admin group first.

Recommendation.Text: Restrict privileged Microsoft first-party administration tools to explicitly assigned administrators. Create the service principal if it does not exist, assign only the users or groups who need access, and set **appRoleAssignmentRequired** to `true`. This removes a common post-compromise reconnaissance path.

Notes: Based on Maester control MT.1186. The list of monitored appIds is configurable via entra_privileged_first_party_app_ids in the m365 audit config. These are Microsoft first-party apps and are intentionally NOT filtered by MICROSOFT_FIRST_PARTY_TENANT_IDS.
